{{< include ./_extensions/r-wasm/live/_knitr.qmd >}}

This page runs R inside your browser and works through the same steps the tutorial will use: installing packages, reading the data, and fitting a paired t-test, a linear mixed model and an ordinal mixed model. Everything starts on its own.

::: {.callout-note}
## The first visit is slow

Your browser downloads R and each package the first time, which can take a minute or two. Keep this tab open until the **Summary** at the bottom shows numbers. Later visits are faster because the browser caches the downloads.
:::

## 1. R is running

```{webr}
#| caption: R version
R.version.string
```

## 2. Install the packages

Each package is downloaded from the webR package repository. `available` should be `TRUE` for every row.

```{webr}
#| caption: Install and load packages
pkgs <- c("lme4", "lmerTest", "pbkrtest", "ordinal", "emmeans", "ggplot2")

pkg_status <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pkgs, function(p) {
  secs <- system.time(
    ok <- tryCatch({
      install.packages(p, quiet = TRUE)
      requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)
    }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  )[["elapsed"]]
  data.frame(
    package   = p,
    available = ok,
    version   = if (ok) as.character(packageVersion(p)) else NA_character_,
    seconds   = round(secs, 1)
  )
}))

pkg_status
```

## 3. Load the simulated data

The data copy the design of the study (66 participants, 6 rehearsals each, 3 reports per rehearsal) but are simulated. Expect 1,188 rows, 66 participants and 396 child-behavior reports.

```{webr}
#| caption: Read the CSV
affect <- read.csv("data/affect_sim.csv")
cb <- subset(affect, checkpoint == "child_behavior")

c(rows         = nrow(affect),
  participants = length(unique(affect$participant_id)),
  cb_reports   = nrow(cb))
```

## 4. Plot the ratings

Checks that graphics work. Notice how many baseline ratings sit at the top of the scale.

```{webr}
#| caption: Pleasure about the child's behavior
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.5
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ggplot2))
ggplot(cb, aes(factor(pleasure, levels = -4:4), fill = loop_type)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Pleasure rating (-4 to +4)", y = "Reports", fill = "Rehearsal") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Paired t-test

One average difference per participant, as in the early analysis.

```{webr}
#| caption: Paired t-test on participant means
pm   <- aggregate(pleasure ~ participant_id + loop_type, data = cb, FUN = mean)
wide <- reshape(pm, idvar = "participant_id", timevar = "loop_type", direction = "wide")
tt   <- t.test(wide$pleasure.challenge, wide$pleasure.baseline, paired = TRUE)
tt
```

## 6. Linear mixed model

The same comparison, with a participant random intercept and challenge slope. Kenward–Roger degrees of freedom need `pbkrtest`; if it is missing, the page falls back to Satterthwaite.

```{webr}
#| caption: lmer with Kenward-Roger inference
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lmerTest))

lmm_secs <- system.time(
  m_lmm <- lmer(pleasure ~ challenge + (1 + challenge | participant_id),
                data = cb, REML = TRUE)
)[["elapsed"]]

ddf <- if (requireNamespace("pbkrtest", quietly = TRUE)) "Kenward-Roger" else "Satterthwaite"
kr_secs <- system.time(lmm_tab <- coef(summary(m_lmm, ddf = ddf)))[["elapsed"]]

cat("Singular fit:", isSingular(m_lmm), " | df method:", ddf, "\n\n")
print(lmm_tab)

cat("\nBecause the data are balanced, the mixed model's t matches the paired t-test:\n")
print(round(c(paired_t = unname(tt$statistic), lmm_t = lmm_tab["challenge", "t value"]), 3))
```

## 7. Ordinal mixed model

Confusion is rated 1 to 5, so it is modeled as ordered categories with a cumulative logit link. This is the slowest step.

```{webr}
#| caption: clmm for confusion
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(ordinal))
cb$confusion_ord <- ordered(cb$confusion, levels = 1:5)

clmm_secs <- system.time(
  m_clmm <- clmm(confusion_ord ~ challenge + (1 + challenge | participant_id),
                 data = cb, link = "logit", Hess = TRUE, nAGQ = 1)
)[["elapsed"]]

print(summary(m_clmm)$coefficients)
cat("\nOdds ratio for challenge:", round(exp(coef(m_clmm)[["challenge"]]), 2), "\n")
```

## Summary

```{webr}
#| caption: Timings in this browser
step_secs <- function(x) if (exists(x)) round(get(x), 1) else NA

data.frame(
  step    = c("Install packages (total)", "lmer fit", "Kenward-Roger summary", "clmm fit"),
  seconds = c(if (exists("pkg_status")) sum(pkg_status$seconds) else NA,
              step_secs("lmm_secs"), step_secs("kr_secs"), step_secs("clmm_secs")),
  ok      = c(exists("pkg_status") && all(pkg_status$available),
              exists("m_lmm"), exists("lmm_tab"), exists("m_clmm"))
)
```

**What this tells us**

- If every `ok` is `TRUE`, the full tutorial can run in the browser.
- If the `clmm` fit takes more than about 30 seconds, the ordinal modules will fit models ahead of time and load them, so students don't wait.
- If a package shows `available = FALSE`, the module that needs it will show pre-computed output for that step instead.
